Libraries:

```{r}
# Some tips from Sisk:
# https://github.com/msisk1/MtH_NLP/blob/main/MtH_2026.qmd

library(tidyverse)
library(tidytext)
library(textstem)
library(ggrepel)
library(ggwordcloud)
library(ggraph)
library(hunspell)
library(text2vec)
# library(word2vec)
library(reticulate)
library(udpipe)
library(data.table)
library(jsonlite)
library(tinytable)

seed <- 3256L
set.seed(seed)

source("functions.R")
```

Stop words:

```{r}
# Prepare stop words
# Remove a few words from the stop word list that are actually informative
# and add a few new stop words. Removing the "onix" stop words automatically
# removes these.
retain <- c(
  "man",
  "men",
  "group",
  "groups",
  "grouping",
  "grouped",
  "work",
  "works",
  "working",
  "worked",
  "area",
  "areas"
)

stop_words2 <-
  stop_words |>
  dplyr::filter(lexicon != "onix") |>
  filter(!word %in% retain) |> # Just in case
  add_row(word = c("pp", "set", "call"), lexicon = "Added") # add new stop words
```

Load the text from the internet or a saved version, tokenize and lemmatize

```{r}
# Get text version of MTH from Internet Archive
# Different formats: https://archive.org/download/ManTheHunter

if (!file.exists("man-the-hunter.txt")) {
  mth_raw <- read_lines(
    "https://archive.org/download/ManTheHunter/Man%20the%20Hunter_djvu.txt"
  )
  write_lines(mth_raw, file = "man-the-hunter.txt")
} else {
  mth_raw <- read_lines("man-the-hunter.txt")
}

# Remove frontmatter, and references
preface <- 75
main_text_start <- 746
references <- 36991
mth0 <-
  mth_raw[main_text_start:references] |>
  str_replace_all("‘|’", "'") |>
  str_replace_all("“|”", '"') |>
  str_squish() |>
  # Remove the volume title, mentioned throughout
  # the text, per discussion with Sisk
  str_replace_all(regex("Man the Hunter", ignore_case = T), "MTH")

# Remove running titles for the same reason
source("running_titles.R") # Character vector of running titles

for (running_title in running_titles) {
  rx <- paste0("^\\d*\\s*", running_title)
  mth0 <- mth0[!str_detect(mth0, regex(rx, ignore_case = T))]
}

# Try to fix words hyphenated
# at the end of lines
mth <-
  str_flatten(mth0, " ") |>
  str_squish() |>
  str_replace_all("- ", "-") |>
  str_split_1(" ") |>
  dehyphenate() |>
  str_flatten(" ") |>

  # Some manual fixes
  str_replace_all("ofarcheological", "of archeological") |>
  str_replace_all("archeo", "archaeo") |>
  str_replace_all("Archeo", "Archaeo") |>
  str_replace_all("per cent", "percent") |>
  str_replace_all("wor ld", "world") |>
  str_replace_all("IKung", "!Kung") |>
  str_replace_all("Turn-bull", "Turnbull") |>
  str_replace_all("Wood-burn", "Woodburn") |>
  str_replace_all("Wash-burn", "Washburn") |>
  str_replace_all(
    regex("hunters and gatherers", ignore_case = T),
    "hunter-gatherer"
  )

# Tokenizer and lemmatizer using a model that retains hyphenated words
ud_model <- udpipe_load_model(file = "english-gum-ud-2.5-191206.udpipe")
out_udpipe <- udpipe(mth, ud_model)
```

Check if any common stop words are important and should be removed from the stopword list

```{r}
sort(
  table(out_udpipe$lemma[out_udpipe$lemma %in% stop_words2$word]),
  decreasing = T
)[1:150]
```

Remove stopwords

```{r}
lemmas_udpipe0 <-
  out_udpipe |>
  rename(word = token, pos = upos) |>
  mutate(lemma = str_to_lower(lemma)) |>
  anti_join(stop_words2, by = join_by(lemma == word))
```

Top hyphenated words

```{r}
lemmas_udpipe0 |>
  dplyr::filter(str_detect(lemma, "-")) |>
  summarise(N = n(), .by = lemma) |>
  arrange(desc(N)) |>
  dplyr::filter(N >= 5)
```

Modify the `clean_lemmas` function to aggregate a few of these and then create bigrams

```{r}
lemmas_udpipe <-
  lemmas_udpipe0 |>
  clean_lemmas() |> # See functions.R
  mutate(
    next_lemma = txt_next(lemma),
    bigram = paste(lemma, next_lemma)
  )
```

```{r}
# Cleaned up text
write(mth, "mth_clean.txt")
mth_length <- str_count(mth) + 10
```

Lemmas from spaCy using the cleaned up text `mth`

```{python}
import spacy

spacy.util.fix_random_seed(r.seed)
nlp = spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")
nlp.max_length = r.mth_length
doc = nlp(r.mth)
```

```{r}
doc2 <- iterate(py$doc)
lemmas_spacy <-
  tibble(
    word = map_chr(doc2, \(token) token$text),
    lemma = map_chr(doc2, \(token) str_to_lower(token$lemma_)),
    pos = map_chr(doc2, \(token) token$pos_)
  ) |>
  anti_join(stop_words2, by = join_by(lemma == word)) |>
  clean_lemmas()

# Reconstruct the full text as a single string
mth_spacy <- str_flatten(lemmas_spacy$lemma, collapse = " ")
```

Count lemmas

```{r}
# Count lemmas
mth_words_spacy <-
  lemmas_spacy |>
  group_by(lemma) |>
  summarise(n = n()) |>
  arrange(desc(n))

mth_words_udpipe <-
  lemmas_udpipe |>
  group_by(lemma) |>
  summarise(n = n()) |>
  arrange(desc(n))

# See functions.R
lemmas_sisk <-
  sisk_lemmas(mth0) |>
  rename(lemma = word, word = word_orig) |>
  anti_join(stop_words2, by = join_by(lemma == word))

mth_words_sisk <-
  lemmas_sisk |>
  group_by(lemma) |>
  summarise(n = n()) |>
  arrange(desc(n))
```

Identifying major discrepancies. "cent" is mostly from "per cent" in the raw text; I unified the spelling of "archaeology", etc.; "brown" is mostly references to Radcliffe-Brown. "cross" mostly appears in the hyphentated "cross-cultural" or "cross-cousin". The udpipe lemmatizer retains "hunter-gatherer" as a single lemma. The Sisk lemmatizer often maps "number" to "numb", and many words to "good". Other discrepancies were addressed by iterating parts of the pipeline many times and making corrections in the `clean_lemmas` function.

```{r}
mth_words_combined <-
  full_join(mth_words_spacy, mth_words_udpipe, by = 'lemma') |>
  full_join(mth_words_sisk, by = 'lemma') |>
  rename(
    n_spacy = n.x,
    n_udpipe = n.y,
    n_sisk = n
  ) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    sd = sd(c(n_spacy, n_udpipe, n_sisk)),
    cv = sd / mean(c(n_spacy, n_udpipe, n_sisk))
  )

mth_words_discrepancies <-
  mth_words_combined |>
  dplyr::filter(
    cv > 0.25,
    n_spacy > 50 | n_udpipe > 50 | n_sisk > 50
  )

tt(arrange(mth_words_discrepancies, desc(cv)))
```

Compare frequencies of 200 most frequent words in spaCy and udpipe. Large discrepancies in hunter and gather are due, in part to the retention of the hyphenated "hunter-gatherer" in the udpipe version. Some of the biggest discrepancies were already addressed in the `clean_lemmas` function (see `functions.R`).

```{r}
d <-
  mth_words_combined |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(sd)) |>
  arrange(desc(n_udpipe))

ggplot(d[1:200, ], aes(n_spacy, n_udpipe, label = lemma)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text_repel(max.overlaps = 50) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0) +
  #   scale_x_log10() +
  #   scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "spaCy lemma count", y = "udpipe lemma count") +
  coord_fixed()
```

The Sisk lemmatizer maps "number" to "numb", and many more words to "good" than does the udpipe lemmatizer

```{r}
ggplot(d[1:200, ], aes(n_sisk, n_udpipe, label = lemma)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text_repel(max.overlaps = 50) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0) +
  labs(x = "Sisk lemma count", y = "udpipe lemma count") +
  coord_fixed()
```

Network co-occurence

```{r}
bigram_graph <-
  lemmas_udpipe |>
  count(lemma, next_lemma, sort = T) |>
  dplyr::filter(n >= 15) |>
  igraph::graph_from_data_frame()

plot_graph <-
  ggraph(bigram_graph, layout = "fr") +
  # Edge width matches bigram frequency.
  geom_edge_link(
    aes(edge_width = n), # edge_alpha = n,
    edge_alpha = 0.5,
    show.legend = TRUE,
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(3, 'mm')), # Shows phrase directionality
    end_cap = circle(3, 'mm')
  ) + # Stops arrow hiding under the node text

  # Draw the nodes (individual words)
  geom_node_point(color = "skyblue", size = 2) +

  # Overlay readable text labels onto the nodes
  geom_node_text(
    aes(label = name),
    # vjust = 1.5,
    # hjust = 0.5,
    check_overlap = F,
    repel = T,
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 4
  ) +
  # scale_edge_alpha(name = "Co-occurrence Frequency") +
  scale_edge_width(range = c(0.5, 2.5)) + # , guide = "none"
  theme_void() + # Removes axes, ticks, and background grid lines
  labs(
    title = "Word Co-occurrence Network Graph",
    subtitle = "Visualizing bigram relationships and central key terms"
  )
plot_graph
ggsave("networkgraph.pdf", plot_graph)
```

Word vectors from Wiki Giga 2024. Find vectors of top 200 words from MTH relative to a large corpus of text from Wikipedia and newswire text such as the Associated Press (AP), Agence France-Presse (AFP), The New York Times, and the Xinhua News Agency.

```{r}
# Word embeddings: Wiki GIGA 2024
glove_raw <- fread(
  "wiki_giga_2024_100_MFT20_vectors_seed_2024_alpha_0.75_eta_0.05.050_combined.txt",
  header = FALSE,
  data.table = FALSE,
  encoding = "UTF-8"
)
glove_words <- glove_raw[, 1]
glove_matrix <- as.matrix(glove_raw[, -1])

# Assign the words as row names for fast lookup matrices
rownames(glove_matrix) <- glove_words
rm(glove_raw)

# Vectors for top 200
# Using spaCy because glove_words does not contain "hunter-gatherer"

wikivec200 <- glove_matrix[mth200spacy$lemma, ]
rm(glove_matrix)
```

Dimension reduction for plotting

```{python}
import pacmap

reducer1 = pacmap.PaCMAP(
    n_components=2,  # Coordinates for 2D plotting
    distance="angular",
    apply_pca=True,
    n_neighbors=None,  # Default is 10; None: auto-selection
    MN_ratio=0.5,  # Mid-near neighbors ratio (default: 0.5)
    FP_ratio=2.0,  # Further-away pairs ratio (default: 2.0)
    lr=1.0,  # Learning rate
    num_iters=450,  # Default is 450 (100 mid, 200 far, 150 local)
    random_state=r.seed,
)
embedding1 = reducer1.fit_transform(r.wikivec200)
```

Plot

```{r}
mth200 <- as_tibble(wikivec200, rownames = "lemma")
mth200$n <- mth200spacy$n
mth200$e1 <- py$embedding1[, 1]
mth200$e2 <- py$embedding1[, 2]
fn <- "wordcloud.wiki.svg"
plot_vectors(mth200, fn)
```

![](`{r} fn`)

text2vec using udpipe sentences as the documents:

```{r}
# text2vec word embeddings (GlobalVectors)
mth_udpipe <-
  lemmas_udpipe |>
  summarise(
    sentence = str_flatten(lemma, " "),
    .by = sentence_id
  )
it <- itoken(mth_udpipe$sentence)
vocab <- create_vocabulary(it)
vocab <- prune_vocabulary(vocab, term_count_min = 5L)
vectorizer <- vocab_vectorizer(vocab)
# use window of 5-10 for context words
tcm <- create_tcm(it, vectorizer, skip_grams_window = 8L)
glove <- GlobalVectors$new(rank = 30, x_max = 5)
wv_main <- glove$fit_transform(
  tcm,
  n_iter = 100,
  convergence_tol = 0.001,
  n_threads = 1
)
wv_context <- glove$components
word_vectors <- wv_main + t(wv_context)

text2vec200 <- word_vectors[mth200udpipe$lemma, ]
```

Reduce dimensionality

```{python}
reducer2 = pacmap.PaCMAP(
    n_components=2,  # Coordinates for 2D plotting
    distance="angular",
    apply_pca=False,
    n_neighbors=None,  # Default is 10; None: auto-selection
    MN_ratio=0.5,  # Mid-near neighbors ratio (default: 0.5)
    FP_ratio=2.0,  # Further-away pairs ratio (default: 2.0)
    lr=1.0,  # Learning rate
    num_iters=450,  # Default is 450 (100 mid, 200 far, 150 local)
    random_state=r.seed,
)
embedding2 = reducer2.fit_transform(r.text2vec200)
```

Plot

```{r}
mth200 <- as_tibble(text2vec200, rownames = "lemma")
mth200$n <- mth200udpipe$n
mth200$e1 <- py$embedding2[, 1]
mth200$e2 <- py$embedding2[, 2]

```
